raw_case_text:
This study involved a 75-year-old female who was being treated with prednisolone 15 mg daily for interstitial pneumonia and rheumatoid arthritis. She had a history of herpetic and FK in her left eye that was successfully treated with acyclovir eye ointment, natamycin eye ointment, and oral itraconazole. However, she was referred to our hospital due to the fungal corneal infection in her left eye recurring with a deep corneal infiltrate.
At initial presentation, the best-corrected visual acuity in her infected left eye was 30-cm hand motion, and corneal ulcers and infiltration on the temporal side, as well as posterior corneal plaque, were observed. For daily treatment, she was prescribed miconazole 0.1% (every 2 h), gatifloxacin (6 times daily), 1% natamycin ophthalmic ointment (6 times daily), and oral voriconazole (300 mg). Although a reduction in the size and density of the deep corneal infiltration was initially obtained (Fig. 1a), corneal perforation and iris herniation occurred 3 weeks after the initial examination. Moreover, fibrin formation was found around the pupil area and along to the corneal infiltration (Fig. 1b). Since it appeared that a conservative treatment would be difficult, AMT with debridement around the perforated area was performed (Fig. 2). At the 5-month postoperative period, there were no signs of fungal infection, so the natamycin ophthalmic ointment and miconazole were discontinued, and treatment was switched to only a 4-times daily administration of gatifloxacin. However, at the 6-month postoperative period, an increase of keratic precipitates was observed (Fig. 3a). Since she had a history of herpetic keratitis, we suspected recurrent herpetic keratitis, yet polymerase chain reaction test results of anterior-chamber aqueous humor samples for herpes simplex virus, varicella-zoster virus, and cytomegalovirus were all negative. Thus, in consideration of a possible recurrence of fungal infection in her left eye, treatment with oral voriconazole, natamycin ophthalmic ointment (twice daily), and miconazole (twice daily) was resumed. At the 7-month postoperative period, a further increase of keratic precipitates was observed, and adhesion of a pigmentary and white substance was observed on the amnion endothelial surface (Fig. 3b). We suspected the possibility of recurrent fungal infection, so anterior-chamber irrigation was performed in the 9-month postoperative period. Yeast-like fungi were detected (Fig. 3c) via Fungiflora Y staining of the aqueous humor, and Candida species were identified from culture. At the 11-month postoperative period, anterior-segment optical coherence tomography imaging revealed a high intensity of endothelial plaque material beneath the AMT region (Fig. 3e). Intravenous voriconazole and multiple injections of 1 mug/mL voriconazole into the anterior chamber (Fig. 3d) were ineffective, so at 1 year post-AMT, penetrating keratoplasty was performed. Postsurgery, polymerase chain reaction testing showed a positive finding for fungal deposition in the posterior cornea, and immunohistochemistry of a specimen using Fungiflora Y staining revealed fungal deposition throughout the posterior plaque between the transplanted AM and the residual stroma (Fig. 4).
The postoperative course was good, and pimaricin and miconazole were gradually decreased. At 1.5 years post-penetrating keratoplasty, no recurrence of fungal infection was found, and the best-corrected visual acuity in her left eye was 6/60 (Fig. 5).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 75-year-old female on chronic oral prednisolone was referred for recurrent deep fungal keratitis with a temporal corneal ulcer, deep stromal infiltrate, and posterior corneal plaque in her left eye (visual acuity 30-cm hand motion).
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Maintained on oral prednisolone 15 mg/day for interstitial pneumonia and rheumatoid arthritis and having a prior history of left-eye herpetic and fungal keratitis, the patient developed a deep temporal corneal infiltrate with posterior plaque that progressed after 3 weeks of topical 0.1% miconazole, gatifloxacin, 1% natamycin ointment, and oral voriconazole (300 mg) to corneal perforation and iris herniation, treated with debridement and amniotic membrane transplantation (AMT). Topical antifungals were discontinued 5 months post-AMT, but keratic precipitates and a retro-corneal white/pigmented endothelial plaque increased at 6 and 7 months, persisted despite anterior chamber irrigation at 9 months and intravenous/intracameral voriconazole at 11 months, and required therapeutic penetrating keratoplasty (PKP) at 1 year post-AMT.
subjective.past_medical_history: Interstitial pneumonia and rheumatoid arthritis treated with oral prednisolone 15 mg/day; prior history of herpetic keratitis and fungal keratitis in the left eye.
subjective.review_of_systems: Negative for extraocular symptoms. Home medications included oral prednisolone 15 mg/day.

objective.physical_examination: Initial left-eye best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) was 30-cm hand motion (improving to 6/60 at 1.5 years post-PKP). Slit-lamp examination of the left eye revealed a temporal corneal ulcer with deep stromal infiltration and a posterior corneal plaque, progressing at 3 weeks to corneal perforation with iris incarceration and pupillary fibrin, and at 6-7 months post-AMT to increasing keratic precipitates and a retro-corneal white/pigmented endothelial plaque beneath the transplanted amniotic membrane.
objective.advanced_workup: At 6 months post-AMT, anterior chamber aqueous humor PCR was negative for HSV, VZV, and cytomegalovirus (CMV). At 9 months post-AMT, aqueous humor Fungiflora Y staining demonstrated yeast-like fungi and culture grew Candida species; 11-month anterior-segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT) showed a hyperintense endothelial plaque beneath the AMT. Histopathology and fungal PCR of the corneal button excised during penetrating keratoplasty at 1 year post-AMT confirmed fungal DNA and Fungiflora Y-positive fungal elements trapped between the transplanted amniotic membrane and residual posterior corneal stroma.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Recurrent deep Candida keratitis/endophthalmitis with retro-corneal endothelial plaque and corneal perforation in a corticosteroid-treated patient with rheumatoid arthritis, confirmed by aqueous humor Fungiflora Y staining, Candida culture, and PKP corneal button fungal PCR and histochemistry (with HSV, VZV, and cytomegalovirus [CMV] excluded by negative aqueous humor PCR). Following failure of amniotic membrane transplantation and intracameral/systemic voriconazole, therapeutic penetrating keratoplasty at 1 year post-AMT combined with tapered topical pimaricin and miconazole eradicated the infection and restored left-eye BCVA to 6/60 without recurrence over 1.5 years of follow-up.
